_doc: The team the lead (the main session) can hand work to. A role is a brief and a way of working, not a standing agent: most roles are hats the lead wears. 'gw team' lists the roles this project needs, the tasks that can run in parallel, and the token cost against one agent doing everything. 'when' is a list of alternatives; every key in one alternative must match. Costs are ranges from the sources below, not measurements of this project: measure with 'gw team log'.

lead.title: Project manager (lead)
lead.does: plans, orders the tasks, hands work off by its shape, integrates one task at a time, runs the gates and talks to the user. Never delegated.

roles.title: Code reviewer
roles.how: one fresh subagent (required at standard and large)
roles.brief: Review the diff since the baseline against the PRD/FSD sections and the tasks you are given, not the chat. Report only real problems: correctness, security, data loss, missing or weak tests, unmet requirements. Give each one file:line, a severity and why. No style nits. Do not edit files.

roles.title: Security analyst
roles.how: inline for the SRD (P5); one fresh subagent for the security review (P9)
roles.brief: Check the change against docs/srd.md: every SEC- requirement and TH- threat it touches, input at trust boundaries, auth, secrets, crypto, files and network. Report each finding with a severity and its SEC/TH ID. Do not edit files.

roles.title: Senior backend engineer
roles.how: inline; at large tier a worker per parallel task
roles.tools: edits in its own git worktree
roles.model: a cheaper model for small, well-specified tasks
roles.brief: Build to the contracts in docs/bsd.md. Validate input at the boundary, keep errors as documented, change schemas expand-then-contract, and test against a real database or service (S1) where practical. Name the REQ/SEC ID in each test. Run the task's check before you report.

roles.title: Senior frontend engineer
roles.how: inline; at large tier a worker per parallel task
roles.tools: edits in its own git worktree
roles.model: a cheaper model for small, well-specified tasks
roles.brief: Build from the approved mockup in docs/dbd.md: every screen state (empty, loading, error, long text), keyboard and screen-reader access (WCAG 2.2 AA), the project's own components. No new design: a change to the look goes back to the mockup. Run the task's check before you report.

roles.title: QA engineer
roles.brief: Own the test strategy: each task's check names its REQ/SEC ID, checks run at each target's release tier (S0-S3), a flaky test is fixed, not retried.

roles.title: Platform and release engineer
roles.brief: Own the build and release path: CI per target (gw ci), the devcontainer, signing and packaging, the release tier each target needs (gw doctor), and rollback.

roles.title: Researcher
roles.how: one subagent per reference or option, in parallel
roles.tools: read-only, plus web search and fetch
roles.brief: Answer the research goal for one reference or option with sources (links, versions, licences), and keep facts apart from guesses. Return a summary, not raw pages.

roles.title: UX panel (PRD personas)
roles.how: one subagent per persona, blind to the other reviews
roles.brief: Review the mockup as one PRD persona, without seeing the other reviews: what this persona cannot do, finds confusing or misses. Do not redesign.

review.basis: a fresh subagent reads the diff and the doc sections it is given, not the build history (Groundwork's estimate)

research.basis: one subagent per reference against one agent researching alone; faster, and better on breadth-first questions

build.basis: tokens of a task built by a parallel worker against the same task built alone, merge included

sources.anthropic-research: Anthropic, How we built our multi-agent research system (2025): +90.2% over one Opus 4 agent on breadth-first research; agents use about 4x the tokens of chat, multi-agent systems about 15x; coding has fewer parallel parts.
sources.kim-scaling: Kim et al., arXiv 2512.08296 (260 configurations, 6 benchmarks): 1.6-6.2x tokens; returns turn negative once one agent already succeeds about 45% of the time; SWE-bench Verified -2.1 to -14.9%.
sources.caid: Geng and Neubig, CAID, arXiv 2603.21489: parallel workers in git worktrees with test-verified merges, PaperBench 57.2 to 63.3 at about 2.0x cost, Commit0-Lite 53.1 to 59.1 at about 4.3x.
sources.mao-subagents: Mao et al., arXiv 2606.10662: Claude Code with subagents 80.0% at $30.88 against 81.7% at $20.31 alone on Terminal-Bench (Opus 5.5).
sources.mast: Cemri et al., MAST, arXiv 2503.13657: multi-agent systems fail in 41-86.7% of runs; a verification step +15.6%, clearer role specification +9.4%.
sources.claude-code-costs: Claude Code docs, costs page: agent teams use about 7x the tokens of a standard session when teammates run in plan mode; use cheaper models for teammates and simple subagent tasks, keep teams small.
